basis: Absent middle phalanges and duplicated thumb phalanx define skeletal involvement; nail dysplasia is a defining feature.
Tetralogy of Fallot is a congenital structural heart disease; no additional organ involvement is established by this record.
Nonsyndromic hearing loss with congenital inner-ear abnormalities and stapes fixation; no separate neurologic or skeletal disease.
Lethal skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia and cataracts each reported in 80-99%. Coarctation omitted: overall 5-29% annotation conflicts with a 2/2 case series.
Autoimmune conjunctival disease causes scarring and visual loss. Other mucosal and skin disease can occur, but involvement in at least 30% is not established here.
Inherited GPI-anchor biosynthesis disorder with defining neurodevelopmental impairment; intellectual disability, developmental delay and seizures reported in 3/3.
High hyperopia is an ocular refractive disorder; no other organ involvement is established.
Platelet dysfunction and oculocutaneous albinism define disease. Restrictive lung dysfunction occurs in 3/7 (~43%), supporting pulmonary involvement despite fibrosis in only 1/7.
Inherited focal dystonia is a neurologic movement disorder; muscle contractions, voice changes and blepharospasm do not establish damage to other organs.
Secondary glaucoma associated with aniridia directly affects the eye and optic nerve.
